subject: Business Models
title: The App Economy
description: A quick, practical guide to The App Economy.

hook.text: Apple launched the App Store in 2008 with 500 apps. By 2024, it had 1.8 million.

buildup.text: Apple takes 30% of every sale. Developers get global distribution; Apple gets a perpetual cut.

discovery.text: The app economy created 2.2 million jobs in the US alone. A new industry from a software update.

twist.text: Epic Games sued Apple over the 30% tax, calling it a monopoly. Courts partially agreed.

climax.text: App stores proved that distribution is power. Control the storefront, tax the economy.

punchline.text: 500 apps became 1.8 million. The storefront won.

quiz.question: What percentage does Apple take from App Store sales?

details.summary: The app economy emerged with Apple's App Store in 2008, creating a new software distribution model where developers reach billions of users through centralized marketplaces..
details.whyItMatters: App stores democratized software distribution but also created powerful gatekeepers who charge 15 to 30 percent commissions on all transactions..
takeaways: Apple's App Store launched in 2008 with 500 apps and now hosts millions
App store commissions of 15 to 30 percent on transactions fund platform operations
Mobile apps created new business categories including ride-sharing and food delivery

faq.question: How did the App Store change software distribution?
faq.answer: Before app stores, software distribution required physical media, retail partnerships, or web downloads with complex installation. App stores provided one-click installation, automatic updates, trusted payment processing, and discovery through search and rankings.

faq.question: Why is the 30 percent app store commission so controversial?
faq.answer: Developers argue the commission is excessive for a distribution service. Epic Games sued Apple, and the EU's Digital Markets Act forced Apple to allow alternative app stores in Europe..
